hypothesis: Retained v7 SSD point8 submits ~100000 DATA requests plus ~12800 FRONTIER writes; ~74000 existing DATA groups show adjacent buffers can share one vectored io_uring WRITEV request. Batch64 has ~11720 DATA buffers in ~8000 groups. Gather adjacent buffers without copying or changing group membership to reduce SSD submission/completion and small-I/O overhead.
candidate: Only active v7 ext-family runtimes request vector aggregation. Inside each already-validated group, merge up to8 physically adjacent DATA buffers per WRITEV, stopping at every FRONTIER gap and never crossing groups. Singletons retain WRITE. Own every original buffer/pin and the stable iovec array until a terminal CQE; ambiguous submit keeps the whole bundle alive. Full combined CQE length required. Preserve bytes,offsets,tickets,resources,parallel scheduling,coalescing,FRONTIER write,whole-file fdatasync and publish ordering. No payload copies,preallocation changes,allocator changes,OS settings or RAM-path selector changes.
initial_ssd: Five four-arm rounds each ext4-point8 100000 puts and ext4-batch64 750000 puts. Eight writers,1KiB values,2GiB SST,sampling every100 point operations or10 batches. Four warmups;odd old_v4,new_v4,old_v7,new_v7;even reverse.30sec initialcooldown,10sec betweenruns.1Hz recognized competing-process audits. Preserve all stalls;no builds,tests,profiles during scoring.

DATA byte counters equal baseline and total retired worker write requests decrease>=5% in at leastone workload. Median paired sync-count ratio<=1.05 in both. These are exploratory acceptance guards,not complete RFC qualification.
